# go: tools: go-tools-check cannot scan the tools module

**Motivation:** the govulncheck step of `src/go/tools.mk` has never produced a
result; it only ever fails.

```make
go-tools-check: GOFLAGS = $(TOOLFLAGS)
go-tools-check:
	$(AT) cd tools; \
	go mod verify; \
	govulncheck -tags $(GOTAGS) -test ./...; \
```

Two problems stack up.

1. `GOTAGS` is empty for this target, while `tools.go` sits behind
   `//go:build tools`. Every file is excluded, so the run ends with
   `govulncheck: no packages matched the provided patterns`. Adding
   `go-tools-check: GOTAGS = tools`, as `go-tools-install` already does, is
   necessary but not sufficient.

2. With the tag in place, package loading fails instead:
   `tools.go:8:2: import "github.com/golang/mock/mockgen" is a program, not an
   importable package`. The blank-import idiom is only valid for `go install`
   and `go generate`; `-scan module` reports the same, since it still loads
   packages.

`go mod verify` runs before it, so the target reports success for nothing and
failure for everything else.

## Verification PoC

Scanning the built binaries works today and needs no tools-module loading:

```sh
govulncheck -mode=binary bin/$(go env GOOS)/$(go env GOARCH)/goimports
# No vulnerabilities found.
```

Go 1.24 `tool` directives in `go.mod` (`go get -tool`) are the modern
replacement for the `tools.go` idiom and would make source scanning possible
again.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `go-tools-check` reports actual vulnerability results, or the step is
      removed with the reason recorded.
- [ ] Decide between `-mode=binary` over installed tools and migrating the
      tools module to `go.mod` tool directives.
- [ ] Update `src/go/tools.mk` and regenerate the `dist` Makefiles.

<!-- 2026-09-22T16:34Z https://github.com/octomation/makefiles/issues/80#issuecomment-5780229383
Tried the `tool` directives path in octopot/indexit and it works, so here is
the shape it could take, with what I learned on the way.

First, the option this issue lists as an alternative is not really one:
`-scan module` does not avoid package loading. All four spellings fail —

    govulncheck -scan module ./...     patterns are not accepted for module only scanning
    govulncheck -scan module .         patterns are not accepted for module only scanning
    govulncheck -scan module           -: build constraints exclude all Go files
    govulncheck -scan module -tags tools
                                       tools.go:8:2: import ".../mockgen" is a program,
                                       not an importable package

Removing tools.go entirely gives `-: no Go files`. Module mode still needs one
loadable package, so the tools.go idiom has to go either way.

What worked, in three edits:

  - tools/go.mod — a `tool (...)` block with the five tools; it now holds the
    requirements instead of the blank imports;
  - tools/tools.go — imports dropped, build tag and the five `//go:generate go
    install` lines kept, since go-tools-install runs them;
  - the recipe — `govulncheck -tags $(GOTAGS) -test ./...` becomes
    `govulncheck -scan module -tags $(GOTAGS)`.

The package is then empty but loadable, so govulncheck reads go.mod and
completes: `all modules verified` / `No vulnerabilities found`, and `go tool`
lists all five.

Two consequences worth knowing before adopting this:

  - `go mod tidy` demotes the five tools to `// indirect`. That is Go's own
    behaviour for tool-only dependencies — reproduced on a clean module built
    with `go get -tool`, not a quirk of our setup. It does mean the
    `{{if not (or .Main .Indirect)}}` selector in go-tools-update stops
    matching anything; that target is already under `TODO:implement`, so
    nothing regresses today, but the two changes should land together.
  - tools.go is generated by egg and carries `DO NOT EDIT`, so this is not a
    Makefile-only change — the generator has to learn the new shape too. That
    is the part I would not decide unilaterally.

Context on urgency: before `GOTAGS = tools` was added, the target was
vacuously green — without the tag `./...` matched no packages at all and
govulncheck exited zero on an empty set. So this is not a regression to
revert; the check simply never ran. In indexit it surfaced as a red
Continuous delivery run, because fast-check pulls go-tools-check and the
release job runs `make fast-check test`.
